reader.title: Lynching of three Mexican men at Los Lunas, New Mexico
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A mob took three men accused of murdering James Little from the jail at Las Lunas and hanged them (A4, A5, A13).
Three jailed men accused of murdering James Little were taken from the calaboose by a 'mob' and hanged to trees without any legal process (A4, A13, A15); the mob acted on the murder accusation.

Two distinct Las Vegas dispatches, the short Denver Republican wire (A4, A5) and the longer dispatch naming the men (A13, A15), agree on the jail seizure and hanging, and the Las Vegas Gazette independently reported the murder and arrests (A1).

summary.text: The lynching of three Mexican men at Los Lunas took place on the night of October 7, 1881, when a mob took three men accused of murdering James Little from the jail at Las Lunas (also spelled Los Lunas), New Mexico Territory, and hanged them.
The killing reached papers from California to Illinois through a brief Denver wire, and one Illinois paper headed it as a "good job" by Judge Lynch.
James Little, a former conductor on the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe railroad, was killed at Las Lunas on the night of Wednesday, October 5.
A special to the Las Vegas Daily Gazette dated October 6 said he had been found murdered that morning "in the bar room," while other accounts placed the killing at his house.
According to the Gazette, Little had thirteen knife wounds and had shot both of his attackers before he fell.
A second Gazette special reported that two men, Selzo Espinose and Aristote Noranjo, had been caught and had confessed.
A later Las Vegas dispatch described the killers as "a party of drunken Mexican desperadoes" and named three men arrested the next morning: Seljo Spinosa, Aristote Naranjo and Fernando Chavez.
On the night of Friday, October 7, a mob took the three prisoners from the calaboose.
They were "strung up to cottonwood trees along the Rio Grande," according to the Las Vegas dispatch, and were found dead there the next morning.
The same dispatch called the mob "quiet and orderly" and said there had been "no good reason" for the murder; no members of the mob were named.
No report of an inquest, an arrest of any member of the mob, or any official response was found in the coverage.

Most papers ran a single sentence from the Denver Republican's Las Vegas special, reporting that the mob took three Mexicans "who a few days ago murdered James Little" from jail and hanged them, which treated the men's guilt as settled.
The item appeared under headlines such as "Hung by a Mob" in the Chicago Tribune, "Speedy Justice" in the Cheyenne Daily Leader and "Life in New Mexico" in the Los Angeles Herald.
Condensed versions ran in news digests in Midwestern and Arizona papers through October 22, sometimes beside other New Mexico lynchings.
The Ottawa Free Trader printed the fuller dispatch under the headline "A Good Job By Judge Lynch," and a Wisconsin weekly review repeated its account, with the river misprinted as the "No Grando."
Every account identified the victims only as "Mexicans," and none questioned the mob's action.
The early Gazette reports named two assailants, while the later dispatch named three men, all of whom were lynched.
A Helena reprint of the Denver wire said the hanging took place "yesterday afternoon," against the night stated in the Las Vegas dispatches.

accounts.gist: Little was found murdered in the bar room on the morning of Oct. 6 with thirteen knife wounds; two men, Espinose and Noranjo, were caught and confessed, both having been shot by Little.

accounts.label: Denver Republican's Las Vegas wire
accounts.gist: On the night of Oct. 7 a mob took three Mexicans who had murdered Little from the jail and hanged them to a tree.

accounts.label: Longer Las Vegas dispatch of Oct. 9
accounts.gist: A party of drunken 'Mexican desperadoes' murdered Little at his house; three named men were arrested, confessed, and were taken from the calaboose by a 'quiet and orderly mob' and hanged to cottonwoods along the Rio Grande.

framing.detail: Most papers ran the one-sentence Denver wire under neutral or flip heads such as 'Hung by a Mob', 'Speedy Justice' and 'Life in New Mexico', treating the men's guilt as settled ('who a few days ago murdered James Little').
The Ottawa Free Trader headed its extract 'A Good Job By Judge Lynch' and printed that 'there was no good reason for the deed' and the mob was 'quiet and orderly'.

versions.value: Two men (Espinose and Noranjo), both shot by Little
A 'party' of drunken Mexicans, three named men arrested and lynched

conflicts.note: The early Gazette and the digest built on it name two assailants; the later dispatch names three, adding Fernando Chavez. The coverage does not explain the third man's role.
Both versions may describe the same building; the papers do not say.
The Helena reprint of the same Denver wire, otherwise garbled ('Los Tunis'), alone says afternoon; the Las Vegas dispatches say night.
